source_records.citation: Manikkam et al. (2012). Transgenerational Actions of Environmental Compounds on Reproductive Disease and Identification of Epigenetic Biomarkers of Ancestral Exposures. PLOS ONE 7(2): e31901.
source_records.version: Published article and linked Supplemental Table S1 (.s007).
verified_locations: Main PDF p. 2 Results: F0-only injection, breeding, and F0/F1/F2 developmental exposure explanation; visually checked.
Main PDF p. 9 treatment and breeding methods; visually checked.
Supplemental Table S1B p. 1 and S1C p. 2, Dioxin row; visually checked cell by cell.
limitations: No individual pedigree was reconstructed. Four F1 weaned litters are not treated as a complete register of all injected F0 dams.
The source's mechanistic and toxicological claims are not benchmark reference conclusions. The generational classification concerns the original exposure window, not measured chemical absence.

limitations: The study also provides individual libraries. Their existence is retained in the evidence; the benchmark claim is explicitly restricted to the pooled arm.

source_records.citation: Yen et al. (2014). Somatic mosaicism and allele complexity induced by CRISPR/Cas9 RNA injections in mouse zygotes. Developmental Biology 393(1):3-9.
source_records.version: NCBI BioC XML of PMC4166609 / NIHMS627582; primary author-manuscript text.
verified_locations: Methods: RNA injections into mouse zygotes and Tyr mutation analysis.
Results: Characterization of CRISPR/Cas9-induced Tyr mutations, including mouse #30 and the 23-founder aggregate.
Results: Germ line transmission of targeted Tyr alleles.
Discussion: Complete albinism and pigmentation mosaicism paragraph, explicitly stating why hybrid mosaics were not tested.

Publisher Figure 3C, Mouse 30: deletion alleles 1-5 and insertion allele 6; visually checked on 2026-09-21. [Publisher Figure 3](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0012160614003133-gr3_lrg.jpg)
limitations: The archived NCBI BioC XML is author-manuscript text. Publisher Figure 3C was retrieved separately and visually inspected; the full publisher text/PDF remains unavailable for version comparison.

The author-manuscript Results paragraph beginning A variety of mutations within exon 4 reports five mutant alleles in mouse #30 and also discusses allele 6. Publisher Figure 3C lists six #30 entries: alleles 1-5 under deletions and allele 6 under insertions. The exact count remains unresolved; both accounts support within-founder mosaicism. The figure column n counts sequenced clones per allele.
The Results and Discussion contain inconsistent insertion/deletion or allele-effect wording for C57BL/6N mouse #14; that sequence-level interpretation is excluded.
The 5% reporting threshold does not enumerate every allele or cell. No F1 sequence dataset was reanalysed.
